title: Korean, Slovakian partnership for financing nuclear projects
html:
Export-Import Bank of Slovakia (Eximbanka) is Slovakia's only public export credit agency responsible for export financing for national strategic industries, such as cars, energy, and machinery and plant construction.

"This agreement was established to lay the foundation for cooperation between the two countries in the fields of nuclear power and energy infrastructure, and to strengthen the supply chain of related industries, in line with the global trend of strengthening energy security and decarbonisation," Korea Trade Insurance Corporation (K-Sure) said.

It noted that nuclear power is a key energy source in Slovakia, accounting for more than half of its total electricity production. Slovakia is currently actively pursuing the construction of new large-scale nuclear power plants.

"The cooperation between the two organisations is expected to serve as a catalyst to support the expansion of leading domestic nuclear and power companies into Slovakia in the future," the South Korean bank said.

Eximbanka said South Korean companies have extensive international experience in the construction of power generation facilities, including nuclear power plants and small modular reactors (SMRs). "Should they succeed in public tenders related to the construction of a nuclear power plant in Slovakia, Eximbanka and K-Sure are prepared to cooperate in supporting relevant commercial transactions," it said. "The memorandum also provides for the exchange of technical expertise, the identification of financing options, and the exploration of opportunities for co-financing and risk sharing.

"This cooperation is also significant in light of the existing economic ties between Slovakia and South Korea, which is one of the most important foreign investors in Slovakia. Korean companies with a Slovak business registration number may utilise Eximbanka's financial instruments provided they meet the relevant conditions. At the same time, Slovakia represents a potential base for their business activities in the broader region of Central and Eastern Europe."

It added that opportunities for cooperation are also emerging in the area of involving Slovak subcontractors in overseas projects undertaken by Korean companies, "including EPC+F projects, which combine the implementation of an investment project with securing financing".

Slovakia currently has five nuclear reactors generating more than half its electricity, with one more reactor currently under commissioning. The first two, at Bohunice, went into commercial operation in 1984 and 1985, respectively, while Mochovce 1 and 2 were connected to the grid in 1998 and 1999, respectively. Construction of Mochovce 3 and 4 began in 1986 but was halted in 1992. It was later restarted, and Mochovce 3 entered service in 2023, with Mochovce 4 expected to be operating at full power within the next few months.

"Slovakia is a key nuclear power country in Eastern Europe and a market with high potential for Korean companies to enter," said K-Sure President Jang Young-jin. "We will continue to provide unsparing financial support to enable our companies with excellent technology to participate in the European energy supply chain."
summary: Korea Trade Insurance Corporation has signed a memorandum of understanding with Export-Import Bank of Slovakia to support power and utility projects - including nuclear power plants - and the strengthening of related supply chains.
